gen_risks.description: Incremental deployment of initial anchor projects leaves spare storage capacity, creating a risk of T&S network underutilisation and revenue support exposure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run the HyNet top-up process to recruit additional industrial emitters and fill remaining network storage capacity.
gen_risks.evidence: introduces a risk of network underutilisation and revenue support exposure, but represents the most effective way to deploy CCUS.

gen_risks.description: Executing T&S FID prior to anchor capture projects achieving FID creates financial exposure and schedule mismatch risks if capture projects fail to close.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict financial and permitting conditions precedent on anchor projects prior to contract finalisation.
gen_risks.evidence: We plan to execute Eni’s FID (T&S FID) first with Protos and EETH taking their FIDs afterwards.

gen_risks.description: Low UK ETS carbon market prices fail to provide adequate private sector incentive to invest in carbon capture without long-term government subsidies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long-term CfD-style revenue support contracts to guarantee strike price coverage over key operational periods.
gen_risks.evidence: The Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment, there is a first-mover disadvantage due to high start-up costs

gen_risks.description: Risk of CO2 leakage from deep offshore geological storage reservoirs in Liverpool Bay causing environmental harm and financial liabilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Underwrite key leakage liabilities via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement and install offshore sentinel and monitoring wells.
gen_risks.evidence: government will underwrite several key high-impact, low-probably risks – principally relating to CO2 leakage – via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA).

gen_risks.description: Capital expenditure overruns during Eni's construction of the onshore and offshore T&S network could inflate cluster deployment costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply a regulatory cost-sharing mechanism where the T&SCo recoups only 40% of expenditure exceeding the agreed regulatory capital baseline.
gen_risks.evidence: overruns against this allowance subject to a cost sharing factor; the T&SCo will only recoup 40% of any costs in excess of the agreed level.

gen_risks.description: Escalating costs of industrial emissions without available CCUS infrastructure could force energy-intensive manufacturers to relocate outside the UK.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate CCUS cluster deployment and industrial business model subsidies to safeguard domestic industrial competitiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: manufacturers of critical industrial materials may relocate to more favourable jurisdictions due to the escalating costs of emissions; otherwise known as ‘carbon leakage’.

gen_risks.description: Delays in final funding approval beyond time-limited supplier bids force developers to re-negotiate vendor contracts, driving up costs and causing schedule slippage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Progress approvals ahead of the Spending Review or negotiate bid extensions directly with supply chain partners.
gen_risks.evidence: If the approval of the FFE is delayed we would need to postpone FID and developers would need to re-negotiate supplier bids.

gen_risks.description: Complex cross-chain interdependencies between the T&SCo and capture projects risk financial and operational disruption if network downtime or outages occur.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted government underwriting for cross-chain risks and establish oversight via the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function.
gen_risks.evidence: learnings from the cancelled second CCUS competition in 2016 showed that private sector developers and insurers are not yet ready to bear the ‘cross-chain’ risks

gen_risks.description: Dispersing post-FID contract management across DESNZ, Ofgem, LCCC, and CGL introduces governance coordination risks and operational friction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function to coordinate cross-body operations and execute defined Integrated Processes.
gen_risks.evidence: No single party is suitable to manage all of these agreements, and so contract management responsibilities are dispersed across multiple organisations.

gen_risks.description: Shortfalls in network demand or user fees trigger exchequer payout liabilities under the Revenue Support Agreement to cover T&S allowed revenues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Regular monitoring by LCCC and DESNZ alongside top-up emitter onboarding to maintain adequate T&S network flow volumes.
gen_risks.evidence: If there was a shortfall in demand for the network, and aggregate user fees did not meet the T&SCos allowed revenue, government guarantees these fees

gen_risks.description: Build-out projects (Padeswood and Viridor) failing or delaying taking FID results in prolonged T&S network underutilisation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Agree Statements of Principles early and enforce delivery maturity requirements prior to individual build-out FBC approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: risk that if one or more of the build-out projects in HyNet fails to take FID, the network as a whole will be underutilised

gen_risks.description: Partner ALBs and regulators may lack the staffing capacity and specialized capability required for effective post-FID administration.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require Organisational Readiness Statements and run pre-FID checkpoints to identify and resolve resource or skill gaps.
gen_risks.evidence: To assess capacity and capability of key partner organisations to deliver their roles at FID, the CCUS programme commissioned partner organisations... Organisational Readiness Statements.

gen_risks.description: Constraints in supply chain capacity and specialized vendor availability drive up equipment procurement costs and delay delivery dates.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage external technical advisors, manage procurement schedules incrementally, and engage key vendors early.
gen_risks.evidence: Given the limited supplier market capability, and loss of confidence in the UK CCUS vision, underlying costs are expected to increase.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that government (HMG) is exposed to increased costs for Track-1 post-Financial Investment Decision (FID), and that cost pressures are unaffordable within delegated budgets. [Strategic Case risk T1SR1, Section 2.5 'Identify high level potential risks', p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Contractual mechanisms ensure HMG only takes on specific risks where appropriate, with liability limited and counterparties incentivised to control costs; governance mechanisms monitor costs and provide early warning of overruns; contingent liability exposure is accurately monitored.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the programme does not realise its intended benefits for Track-1. [Strategic Case risk T1SR3, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Projects undergo detailed technical assurance and financial due diligence; projects must meet Initial Conditions Precedent (ICPs) before contracts take effect and Operational CPs thereafter, with LCCC able to terminate and avoid paying for an underperforming project; contractual mechanisms allocate performance-related risk to the private sector; continued engagement with the global Carbon Management Challenge to expand CCUS use and deliver UK trade benefits.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk that the post-FID operating model across public and private sector parties will not operate successfully. [Strategic Case risk T1SR4, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: Medium/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Progress of arm's-length bodies' (ALBs') capacity (funding, resource) and capability (knowledge, skills) to operate successfully post-FID is monitored through the Delivery Board; a DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function will be set up between FID and Commercial Operations Date (COD) to mitigate risks to cluster delivery and system integration; readiness-testing mechanisms are in place ahead of FID; FY24/25 funding for the ALBs to fulfil their roles has been secured.

gt_risks.description: There is a risk of an unclear exit path for HMG from its role in the Track-1 commercial framework. [Strategic Case risk T1SR5, Section 2.5, p.20-21; source rating: High/Possible.]
gt_risks.mitigation: Key planned developments include amendments to the process for granting economic licences, a move toward a competitive allocation process for capture contracts, and evolution of transport & storage business models to reflect an increased private-sector role in managing cross-chain risks; cost-reduction levers (UK ETS pricing, CBAMs) are intended to help cultivate a self-sustaining industry and enable an HMG exit path.
